text:
New Jersey put three goals past Logan Thompson in the third period, and the one that broke a 2-2 tie was the least likely of the night. Vladislav Kolyachonok, a defenseman the Panthers drafted 52nd overall in 2019, scored on a chance our model gave less than a 1% shot of going in. Stefan Noesen and Jack Hughes, the latter with 45 seconds left, added to a 5-2 win over Washington at Prudential Center.

The game was not as lopsided as the score. Washington had the better of the chances: 2.56 expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to 2.15 for New Jersey, and our simulations of every shot gave the Capitals a 61% chance to win, meaning they won 61% of the replays. The gap sat in goal. Thompson allowed 2.0 more goals than the 28 shots he faced should have produced, while Connor Hellebuyck stopped 26 of 28 and finished slightly ahead of what was expected. Washington also gave the puck away 21 times to New Jersey's 12, and Alex Ovechkin's best look, a 29% chance in the third, missed the net.

Evan Rodrigues, a free agent who was never drafted, scored the opening power-play goal and assisted on Kolyachonok's. Lenni Hameenaho, a second-round pick out of Finland's Liiga, tied it at 2-2 with a deflection in the second period. These two teams met on Oct. 17 and Washington won 4-2, so New Jersey has answered that one. Nothing in the facts on hand speaks to either team's streak or record, but the Capitals will wonder how a game they controlled got away.
